analysis.title: Sweep-stakes: How To Trade the Democratic Midterm Victory
key_insights: Betting markets put the probability of a Democratic sweep in Tuesday's midterms at 67%. Goldman's playbook is long healthcare and renewables, short Big Pharma, defense, crypto and potentially the AI complex.
The Goldman framing is that the trades depend less on which laws Democrats can pass and more on which sectors become targets of Washington's attention.
NDX has been in a multi-month trading range. King Callahan describes it as 'running very hard to stand very still', and the question raised is whether the midterms break it out of that range.

AI power trade: Democrats want to protect households from rising electricity costs, which could force data centers to carry more of the infrastructure cost. Goldman is long renewables and grid infrastructure and buys protection on hyperscalers and data-center equipment.

Healthcare: Democrats want to revive ACA subsidies, which could raise patient volumes and cut uncompensated care for providers. The offsetting risk is more aggressive drug-price negotiation. Goldman is long ACA beneficiaries and short drugmakers.

Government spending: Democrats have traditionally pushed for domestic spending to rise alongside defense budgets. Goldman sees upside for government contractors, research institutions and healthcare-related spending beneficiaries, and relative pressure on defense-exposed equities. Goldman is long non-defense government spending and short defense beneficiaries.
Regulation: Goldman is short Big Tech on a return of antitrust enforcement, and short investment banks and crypto on more regulators and fewer political allies.
Tariffs: Goldman is short tariff-sensitive stocks. It does not expect Democrats to relieve tariffs and sees more upside than downside risk from tariffs into early 2027.
Housing: Goldman is long homebuilders, citing housing affordability as a political priority and possible expanded housing tax credits and first-time buyer incentives.

Taxes: Goldman sees little immediate earnings risk for 2027-28 because Trump keeps veto power and the 21% corporate tax rate is already permanent. Further out, high-tax companies could face a less favorable valuation backdrop.
